title: OpsAtlas Service manifest, version 1
description: The contract a monitored repository commits as service.yaml. Structural identity is required here; everything a team could reasonably omit is optional and judged by the scorecard instead, so that a manifest can register and then be told what it is missing.

apiVersion.description: Selects the schema version. An unrecognised value is a validation error, never a guess.

name.description: Stable identifier. Becomes the catalog slug and the metrics prefix, so it follows DNS label rules.

displayName.description: Human-facing name. Falls back to name when absent.

owner.description: Slug of the owning team. Optional on purpose: an unowned service must be registerable so the catalog can show that nobody is accountable for it. The owner-declared scorecard check is what reports it.

repository.description: Source repository in owner/name form. Required: it is where this manifest came from, and it keys the service alongside the manifest path.

tier.description: 1 = customer-facing and paged, 2 = business hours, 3 = internal best effort. Required because every tier-conditional policy rule depends on it.

runtime.description: Free-form runtime slug, e.g. spring-boot, node, go, static. Deliberately not an enum: a closed list would reject a new runtime before the catalog could record it.

environments.description: Where this service runs. At least one, and names must be unique - uniqueness is checked after schema validation so the error can point at the offending entry.

journeys.description: Customer-visible experiences this service is on the path for. The one field the platform cannot infer from telemetry, and the reason an on-call engineer can answer 'who is affected' without asking a product manager.

dependencies.description: What this service calls. Absent means 'not stated'; an empty list means 'stated: none'. The scorecard treats those differently.

url.description: Base URL the observer will probe. http is permitted for local and preview environments only; the scorecard is where that judgement belongs, not the schema.

healthPath.description: Absolute path on the environment URL, e.g. /actuator/health/readiness.

serviceName.description: The OpenTelemetry service.name this process reports under. Without it, traces cannot be joined to this catalog entry.

runbook.description: Absolute https URL, or a repository-relative path such as docs/runbook.md.

contact.description: Chat channel or alias that reaches the owning team during working hours. Not an escalation path: see oncall.

oncall.description: How this service is escalated to out of hours. Deliberately a declaration about where the rotation lives and what it covers, never a claim about who is on call right now - OpsAtlas has no paging provider to ask, and a name it could not refresh would be worse than no name. Additive and optional, so every v1 manifest written before this still validates.

rotation.description: Absolute https URL of the schedule, in whatever system owns it - a PagerDuty or Opsgenie schedule, or a wiki page. What matters is that somebody woken at 03:00 can find who is next.

coverage.description: What the rotation actually covers. The load-bearing field: a tier 1 service whose rotation is business-hours only is a stated gap, and stating it is better than a scorecard that cannot see it.

escalation.description: Where a page goes if the first responder does not answer. Free text, because this is a team name as often as a URL.

availability.description: Target availability as a percentage. Exclusive of 100: a 100% target has no error budget, which makes every alert threshold undefined.

window.description: Rolling window the target is measured over, in whole days, e.g. 30d.

dependency.description: Either a bare string, which is shorthand for kind: service, or an object naming the kind explicitly.

kind.description: service = another registered OpsAtlas service; datastore = a database, cache or queue; external = a third party outside the organisation.
